A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CRAMF research and are readable, including equations, tables and image-based figures. The supplied v1 ends after its references; v2 includes Appendices A–E. The retained and added material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Tables 1–6 report original autoformalization, retrieval and ablation results on miniF2F, ProofNet, AdvancedMath and CombMath.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experiments and adds evaluated models, retrieval comparisons, case studies, statistical tests and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The knowledge-base construction, conditional rewriting, contextual query enhancement, hybrid retrieval and top-10/top-5/top-3 selection procedure are retained. MCP and DCR are relabeled MCE and DHR. Expanded prompts and implementation descriptions do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same mathematical formalization coverage through miniF2F, ProofNet, AdvancedMath and CombMath. V2 documents AdvancedMath's textbook source and subject composition, but does not establish a change to its represented data or tasks.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add Gemini 2.5 Flash, Claude 4.1 and Godel-V2-8B to the four original autoformalizers. Tables 3–4 add LeanExplore, LeanSearch and Dependency Retrieval alongside BM25, R3 and HyDE. This substantially broadens the evaluated comparison methods, including specialized Lean retrieval systems.

E3.justification: Section 3.1.3 changes HitRate@K from requiring a retrieved definition scoring at least 2 to requiring an exact-match score of 3, substantively changing retrieval success. Appendix E additionally introduces batch-size-1 latency and context-budget evaluations. Newly disclosed configurations in Appendix B do not establish changes to the original experiments or reruns.

E4.justification: The component and rewriting ablations in Tables 5–6 are retained. Appendix A.2 adds detailed rewriting, compilation-failure and semantic-consistency case comparisons, while Appendix E adds module-level latency and context-overhead analyses. These substantially expand the questions investigated beyond the original ablations and introductory examples.

E5.justification: Appendix A.1 introduces paired per-problem Wilcoxon tests, sample counts, test statistics, p-values and a significance threshold of 0.01 for twelve original model–dataset combinations. Table 10 newly reports latency standard deviations and ranges. Neither version establishes independent-seed replication or an increase in repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: Existing numerical rows in Tables 1–6 are retained, while Tables 1–4 add substantial results for new comparators. For example, Godel-V2-8B achieves miniF2F FAR@10 of 88.1% without and 95.1% with CRAMF. Appendices add case outcomes, statistical results and latency/token measurements. Retained HitRate values have a changed stated metric, preventing a straightforward same-setting interpretation.

T1.justification: Equation 2 changes the mathematical definition of HitRate@K from max Score ≥ 2 to max Score = 3. The ontology formalization and ACS definition remain unchanged, and no new methodological theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstracts and contribution lists retain the same concept-driven retrieval framework, knowledge-base contribution and plug-and-play improvement claims, including the stated maximum 62.1% and average 29.9% relative improvements. Additional experiments support the existing contribution rather than redefine it.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations for the limitations of LeanSearch, LeanExplore and dependency retrieval, detailed interpretations of compilation and semantic failures, and arguments that gains are systematic and overhead manageable. These substantially expand interpretation. Some new success-case explanations conflict with the displayed formal statements.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C supply inference parameters, hardware, software and Lean/Mathlib versions, and detailed prompt templates absent from the supplied v1 appendix references. V2 also identifies AdvancedMath's source and adds code/dataset access statements and a repository URL. These materially expand reproducibility documentation without proving that underlying settings changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion of Tao et al.'s premise retrieval and citations for new Lean retrieval comparators, Godel, MathBERT and Faiss, while trimming earlier general RAG references. The central positioning around concept-level definition retrieval remains substantially the same.

P1.justification: The existing main-section order and much of the prose are retained. Local rewrites condense explanations, standardize MCE/DHR terminology, remove stray translation boilerplate and update front matter. Numbered subsections, a reproducibility statement and organized appendices improve navigation without extensively rewriting the existing narrative.

P2.justification: V2 switches from a two-column to a single-column layout and repositions the unchanged original three figures. Comparison tables gain rows and revised formatting. Figures 4–19 and Tables 7–12 add extensive case-study, prompt, statistical, configuration and efficiency displays.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially improves documentation and comparison breadth, especially through detailed prompts, configurations and specialized Lean baselines. However, the revised HitRate definition is unresolved against unchanged Table 4 values and contradictory explanatory wording. New validation examples also contain substantive mismatches: Figure 8 substitutes a subgroup-existence theorem for Figure 7's prime-index normal-subgroup problem. These additions improve inspectability while weakening evidential consistency, so the PDFs do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
